title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch page. Its verso, faintly visible, is a typed page of SGA 7 Exp. IX (the monodromy pairing), and the neighbouring 'pages' are that typescript, not continuations of this argument.

The top lines finish a computation. A first attempt, Hom*(τ_N(S)[-i],Q) taken in degree 0, is crossed out. The final chain identifies something (presumably the i-th graded piece of a dual or truncated object) with (Hom*(τ_{N-i}(S),Q))_i ≅ Hom^i(τ_{N-i}(S),Q). Here τ_{N-i} is a truncation of a graded or complex object S, and the shift by i converts a truncation at N into one at N-i.

Next comes a general categorical statement. Write M(C,S) for a category of 'S-objects' (modules or diagrams indexed by S) with values in a category C. Write M^N(C,S) for the full subcategory of objects truncated or bounded at level N, with inclusion i_N : M^N → M.
- If projective limits (underlined lim, i.e. lim←) exist in C, then i_N has an adjoint, written q^N. The manuscript says 'à gauche', but its own ordering of the chain suggests q^N is right adjoint to i_N; a truncation at the other end is meant.
- Grothendieck then dualizes. He uses the isomorphisms M(C,S)° ≅ M(C°,S), restricting to M^N(C,S)° ≅ M_N(C°,S), so opposite categories swap upper and lower truncations.
- Combining the statement for C with the statement for C°, he gets: when C or C° is, say, a Grothendieck category (so both limits and colimits exist), i_N sits in a string of four adjoint functors φ^N, τ^N, i_N, q^N. These are φ^N ⊣ τ^N ⊣ i_N ⊣ q^N, with τ^N the truncation, φ^N its further left adjoint, and q^N the right adjoint.

This is the familiar picture of skeleton/truncation/coskeleton-type adjoint strings for truncated diagram categories, i.e. Kan extensions along an inclusion of indexing categories. Presumably it serves the divided-power de Rham / crystalline setup: truncated (co)simplicial or graded module objects and their duality with Q-coefficients.
errors: The text says i_N admits a LEFT adjoint q^N under existence of lim, but the final ordering φ^N τ^N i_N q^N places q^N as the right adjoint of i_N. Projective limits normally give right adjoints (coskeleton-like), so 'à gauche' is probably a slip, or the adjoint-ordering convention is reversed.
's'insère' should agree in number with 'les foncteurs' (s'insèrent); this is a trivial slip.
The exact meaning of M(C,S), S and the degree indexing cannot be fully determined from this page alone.

ideas.what: Truncation of a graded/complex object and identification Hom^i(τ_{N-i}S, Q) via shift
Inclusion of N-truncated objects into all S-objects in C has adjoints when C has limits/colimits; dualization via M(C,S)° ≅ M(C°,S) yields a four-term adjoint string φ^N ⊣ τ^N ⊣ i_N ⊣ q^N
ideas.modern_name: skeleton/truncation/coskeleton adjoint strings; Kan extensions along a fully faithful inclusion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kan; standard simplicial homotopy theory (sk ⊣ tr ⊣ cosk), SGA 4 Vbis for (co)skeleta
ideas.where_published: Analogous (co)skeleton adjunctions appear in SGA 4 Exp. Vbis (Saint-Donat), not by Grothendieck personally

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine categorical adjunction and duality remarks on scratch paper. The only curiosity is that the paper is recycled from the SGA 7 IX typescript.
transcription_corrections: 's'insère dans une suite de 4 foncteurs adjoints': the 'de 4' is inserted above the line, 'd'adjo-' and 'et était' are struck out, and 'adjoints' continues on the next line.
'φ^N τ^N i_N q^N' is read correctly.
The faint typed text visible through the paper is the SGA 7 IX typescript on the verso, not part of these notes.
